info.title: DropHawk Developer API
info.description:
Product-level prices for PC components, as tracked by DropHawk.

The API needs no key.
Each IP address may make 60 requests a minute on average, in bursts of up to 30.
RateLimit-Limit reports the burst (30), not the per-minute rate.
RateLimit-Remaining and RateLimit-Reset report what is left of the burst and the seconds until it is full again.
They are left off cacheable responses, because a cached response can be served to a different caller and costs nothing.
A request over the limit gets 429 with a Retry-After header in seconds.

One caching rule covers every protocol: a successful GET (an HTTP/JSON GET or HEAD, or a Connect GET) may be cached publicly for 5 minutes, and every other response, any error or POST included, is no-store.
Every response allows cross-origin requests from any web page.
HEAD is answered like GET, without a body.
Query parameters an endpoint does not define are ignored.

One request field is meaningful beyond its endpoint's own: client.
An agent tool that fronts this API, such as the DropHawk MCP server, sends client=mcp so the buy_url it is handed is attributed to that surface.
Any other value, or none, is a direct API call.
It is a query parameter (a body field for batchGet) rather than a header, so it is part of the cache key.

Every HTTP/JSON error is a google.rpc.Status whose details carry a google.rpc.ErrorInfo with domain "drophawk.net" and a reason.
Branch on the reason, not on the message.
Connect and gRPC callers get their protocol's own error model, with the same ErrorInfo whenever the API raised the error.
Errors the RPC framework raises before the API sees a request carry no ErrorInfo: an undecodable body, a request body over 64 KiB (resource_exhausted for an RPC caller, 413 REQUEST_TOO_LARGE over HTTP/JSON; never rate limiting), or an unknown method.

Within v1, changes are additive only: new fields, endpoints, error reasons and withheld reasons may appear, so ignore what you do not recognise.
Removing a field or changing what one means is a new version, served alongside v1 for at least 3 months.

CacheControl.description: "public, max-age=300" on a successful GET; "no-store" on every other response.

Location.description: The surviving Product's URL, relative to the API's origin.

RateLimitLimit.description: The burst a caller may make back-to-back (30). The sustained rate is 60 requests a minute.

RateLimitRemaining.description: Requests left in the caller's burst. Left off cacheable responses.

RateLimitReset.description: Seconds until the caller's burst is full again. Left off cacheable responses.

BadRequest.description: The request cannot be served as sent. Reason INVALID_IDENTIFIER, INVALID_QUERY, INVALID_PAGE_TOKEN, INVALID_PAGE_SIZE, EMPTY_BATCH, BATCH_TOO_LARGE or INVALID_REQUEST.

MovedPermanently.description: The identifier names a Product that was merged into another. Follow Location to the surviving Product.

NotFound.description: Reason PRODUCT_NOT_FOUND when no Product is known by the identifier, or NOT_FOUND when there is no such endpoint.

PayloadTooLarge.description: Reason REQUEST_TOO_LARGE. The request body is over 64 KiB; retrying it cannot succeed.

TooManyRequests.description: Reason RATE_LIMITED. Wait Retry-After seconds before retrying.

identifiers.title: identifiers
identifiers.description:
The Products to get, each a model_slug or a raw model number. At least 1
 and at most 50; each at most 256 bytes. An identifier that is blank, too
 long or has control characters gets an INVALID_IDENTIFIER result without
 failing the others.

client.title: client
client.description:
Which DropHawk surface is asking, so the buy_url it receives is attributed
 to that surface. "mcp" is honoured: the DropHawk MCP server sends it. Any
 other value, or none, means the API itself. The SDK sends nothing. It
 changes only buy_url, and nothing else about the response.

 Never rewrite a buy_url you were given: use it as is.

drophawk.developer.v1.BatchGetProductsRe.title: BatchGetProductsRequest
drophawk.developer.v1.BatchGetProductsRe.description: BatchGetProductsRequest names the Products to get.

results.title: results
results.description:
One result for each requested identifier, in the order requested, so
 results[i] answers identifiers[i]. Always the same length as the request.

drophawk.developer.v1.BatchGetProductsRe.title: BatchGetProductsResponse
drophawk.developer.v1.BatchGetProductsRe.description: BatchGetProductsResponse answers a batch, one result per identifier.

slug.title: slug
slug.description:
The Brand's stable, URL-safe identifier: lowercase letters, digits and
 hyphens only, for example "asus". It is the slug that BrandRef.slug
 carries on a Product.

name.title: name
name.description: The Brand's display name, for example "ASUS".

product_count.title: product_count
product_count.description:
How many Products the Brand has that DropHawk lists. Products that have
 been removed from the catalog do not count.

drophawk.developer.v1.Brand.title: Brand
drophawk.developer.v1.Brand.description: Brand is a maker of Products, with how many Products it has.

slug.title: slug
slug.description:
The Brand's stable, URL-safe identifier: lowercase letters, digits and
 hyphens only, for example "asus". Use it to refer to the Brand; it never
 needs escaping in a URL.

name.title: name
name.description: The Brand's display name, for example "ASUS".

drophawk.developer.v1.BrandRef.title: BrandRef
drophawk.developer.v1.BrandRef.description: BrandRef names the maker of a Product.

slug.title: slug
slug.description:
The ComponentType's stable, URL-safe identifier: lowercase letters, digits
 and hyphens only, for example "gpu". It is the slug that
 ComponentTypeRef.slug carries on a Product.

name.title: name
name.description: The ComponentType's display name, for example "Graphics Cards".

product_count.title: product_count
product_count.description:
How many Products of this class DropHawk lists. Products that have been
 removed from the catalog do not count.

spec_schema.title: spec_schema
spec_schema.description:
The Specs a Product of this class can have, in display order. A Product's
 specs map only ever uses keys listed here, each holding the kind of value
 declared here. Always present; empty for a class with no Specs.

drophawk.developer.v1.ComponentType.title: ComponentType
drophawk.developer.v1.ComponentType.description:
ComponentType is a class of product with the schema of the Specs its
 Products can carry.

slug.title: slug
slug.description:
The ComponentType's stable, URL-safe identifier: lowercase letters, digits
 and hyphens only, for example "gpu".

name.title: name
name.description: The ComponentType's display name, for example "Graphics Cards".

drophawk.developer.v1.ComponentTypeRef.title: ComponentTypeRef
drophawk.developer.v1.ComponentTypeRef.description:
ComponentTypeRef names the class of product a Product belongs to, such as a
 graphics card or a CPU. The ComponentType decides which Specs its Products
 can carry.

date.title: date
date.description: The day, as an ISO 8601 calendar date (YYYY-MM-DD) in UTC.

price.title: price
price.description: The lowest price observed on that day.

is_carried_forward.title: is_carried_forward
is_carried_forward.description:
True for the one point that falls before the 30-day window: the most recent
 earlier day with a price, included so a Product that has not been priced
 inside the window still has a price to chart. It is the price in force when
 the window opened, not an observation inside it. False for every point
 inside the window.

drophawk.developer.v1.DailyLow.title: DailyLow
drophawk.developer.v1.DailyLow.description:
DailyLow is the lowest price observed for a Product on one day.

 It is the lowest across all of the Product's stores, in stock or not, so it
 is not a history of ProductPricing.best_price.

price.title: price
price.description: The price observed on that day.

date.title: date
date.description: The day, as an ISO 8601 calendar date (YYYY-MM-DD) in UTC.

drophawk.developer.v1.DatedPrice.title: DatedPrice
drophawk.developer.v1.DatedPrice.description: DatedPrice is a price together with the calendar day it was observed on.

model_slug.title: model_slug
model_slug.description: The Product's model_slug, or its raw model number. At most 256 bytes.

drophawk.developer.v1.GetProductDailyLow.title: GetProductDailyLowsRequest
drophawk.developer.v1.GetProductDailyLow.description: GetProductDailyLowsRequest names the Product whose daily lows to get.

points.title: points
points.description:
One point per UTC day on which a price was observed, oldest first. Always
 present; empty when withheld, and when the Product has no history.

withheld_reason.title: withheld_reason
withheld_reason.description:
Why points is empty, and itself absent when points is not: "NO_DATA" when
 DropHawk has no price history for the Product, or "MIXED_CURRENCY" when the
 points in this series span more than one currency. More may be added within v1; treat an
 unrecognised reason as the series being unknown.

drophawk.developer.v1.GetProductDailyLow.title: GetProductDailyLowsResponse
drophawk.developer.v1.GetProductDailyLow.description: GetProductDailyLowsResponse is a Product's daily lows over the last 30 days.

model_slug.title: model_slug
model_slug.description: The Product's model_slug, or its raw model number. At most 256 bytes.

client.title: client
client.description:
Which DropHawk surface is asking, so the buy_url it receives is attributed
 to that surface. "mcp" is honoured: the DropHawk MCP server sends it. Any
 other value, or none, means the API itself. The SDK sends nothing. It
 changes only buy_url, and nothing else about the response.

 Never rewrite a buy_url you were given: use it as is.

drophawk.developer.v1.GetProductRequest.title: GetProductRequest
drophawk.developer.v1.GetProductRequest.description: GetProductRequest names the Product to get.

product.title: product
product.description:
The Product. Where HTTP/JSON answers a merged Product with a redirect, an
 RPC client receives the surviving Product here instead, and can tell by its
 model_slug differing from the one requested.

drophawk.developer.v1.GetProductResponse.title: GetProductResponse
drophawk.developer.v1.GetProductResponse.description:
GetProductResponse carries the requested Product. Over HTTP/JSON the response
 body is the Product itself.

drophawk.developer.v1.ListBrandsResponse.title: ListBrandsResponse
drophawk.developer.v1.ListBrandsResponse.description: ListBrandsResponse lists every Brand that has Products.

amount.title: amount
amount.description:
The amount as a non-negative decimal string with exactly two decimal
 places, a "." separator and no digit grouping, for example "1299.00". It is
 a string rather than a JSON number so the value is exact; parse it with a
 decimal type, not a binary float.

currency.title: currency
currency.description: The ISO 4217 three-letter currency code, for example "AUD".

drophawk.developer.v1.Money.title: Money
drophawk.developer.v1.Money.description:
Money is an amount in a single currency.

 Amounts in different currencies are never compared or combined by this API.
 Wherever a value would have to rank prices in more than one currency, it is
 withheld instead, and a withheld reason beside it says so.

model_slug.title: model_slug
model_slug.description:
The Product's identifier: the URL-safe canonical form of its model number,
 lowercase letters, digits and hyphens only, for example "deco-x1500-1-pack"
 for the model number "Deco X1500(1-pack)". DropHawk derives it, and the
 rule is not a plain lowercase-and-strip: some characters stay significant
 ("+" becomes "-plus-", so U-PoE, U-PoE+ and U-PoE++ are three Products).
 Never derive it from model_number yourself, and never assume two model
 numbers name the same Product because they look alike; store and compare
 the model_slug this API returns.

model_number.title: model_number
model_number.description: The manufacturer's model number as DropHawk records it, for display.

component_type.title: component_type
component_type.description: The class of product this is, which decides the keys in specs.

specs.title: specs
specs.description:
The Product's structured attributes, keyed by the Spec keys its
 ComponentType defines, for example "vram" or "boost_clock_mhz". A key is
 present only when DropHawk holds a value for it of the type the
 ComponentType declares; a missing key means the value is unknown. Always
 present, possibly empty.

images.title: images
images.description:
Images of the Product, primary image first. Always present; empty when
 DropHawk has none.

pricing.title: pricing
pricing.description: What the Product sells for now, and has sold for.

url.title: url
url.description:
The Product's page on drophawk.net, for linking a person to the full price
 comparison and history. An absolute URL.

buy_url.title: buy_url
buy_url.description:
A link that sends a buyer to wherever the Product currently has its
 best_price, chosen when the link is followed rather than when this
 response was produced, so it stays right however long it is kept; it
 sends the buyer to the Product's page instead when the Product has no
 best_price at that moment. Always present, whether or not the Product has a
 best_price now. It is on DropHawk's own redirector and never names a
 Retailer, so it is the only way to send a buyer onward from this API.

 The link carries a src and rep query: src says which DropHawk surface
 handed it out, "api" by default and "mcp" when the request sent client=mcp;
 rep is "json", a machine-readable API response (JSON or binary). Use the
 link exactly as given, and never rewrite it. Following it may be answered
 with 404 if the Product has since been removed.

 Attribution stops at the Product page: when the link lands there because
 the Product has no best_price, no click toward a Retailer is recorded.

drophawk.developer.v1.Product.title: Product
drophawk.developer.v1.Product.description:
Product is one physical part at the manufacturer-SKU level, identified by its
 model number, together with what DropHawk currently knows about its price.

 A Product is independent of where it is sold. Prices are aggregated across
 every store DropHawk tracks for it; this API does not name the stores.

url.title: url
url.description:
An absolute HTTPS URL for the image. The URL is immutable: the bytes behind
 it never change, so it can be cached indefinitely.

width.title: width
width.description: The image's width in pixels, at least 1.

height.title: height
height.description: The image's height in pixels, at least 1.

alt_text.title: alt_text
alt_text.description: A text alternative describing the image, for accessibility.

drophawk.developer.v1.ProductImage.title: ProductImage
drophawk.developer.v1.ProductImage.description: ProductImage is one image of a Product.

best_price.title: best_price
best_price.description:
The lowest current price among the stores that have the Product in stock.
 Out-of-stock prices never count. Absent when withheld; see
 best_price_withheld_reason.

best_price_observed_at.title: best_price_observed_at
best_price_observed_at.description:
When best_price was last observed at the store offering it. Absent exactly
 when best_price is.

best_price_withheld_reason.title: best_price_withheld_reason
best_price_withheld_reason.description:
Why best_price is absent, and itself absent when best_price is present:
 "OUT_OF_STOCK" when stores list the Product at a price but none has it in
 stock, "NO_DATA" when no store lists it at a price at all, or
 "MIXED_CURRENCY" when the in-stock prices are in more than one currency.
 More may be added within v1; treat an unrecognised reason as the price
 being unknown.

in_stock_count.title: in_stock_count
in_stock_count.description: How many stores currently have the Product in stock.

all_time_low.title: all_time_low
all_time_low.description:
The lowest daily price ever recorded for the Product at any store, in stock
 or not, and the first day it was recorded at that price. Absent when
 withheld; see all_time_low_withheld_reason.

all_time_low_withheld_reason.title: all_time_low_withheld_reason
all_time_low_withheld_reason.description:
Why all_time_low is absent, and itself absent when all_time_low is
 present: "NO_DATA" when DropHawk has no price history for the Product, or
 "MIXED_CURRENCY" when that history spans more than one currency. More may
 be added within v1; treat an unrecognised reason as the price being
 unknown.

drophawk.developer.v1.ProductPricing.title: ProductPricing
drophawk.developer.v1.ProductPricing.description:
ProductPricing summarises a Product's prices across every store DropHawk
 tracks it at.

 A price DropHawk cannot state is withheld: its field is absent, and the
 matching *_withheld_reason field says why. The withheld reasons, shared by
 every price this API withholds (including a Product's daily lows, which have
 their own withheld_reason), are:

 - "NO_DATA": there is nothing to compute the price from.
 - "OUT_OF_STOCK": stores list the Product at a price, but none has it in
   stock (only for prices that count in-stock stores alone).
 - "MIXED_CURRENCY": the prices it would be computed from are in more than one
   currency, and so cannot be ranked against each other.

 More may be added within v1; treat an unrecognised reason as the price being
 unknown.

identifier.title: identifier
identifier.description:
The identifier exactly as it was sent, so a caller can map the result back
 without relying on position.

product.title: product
product.description: The Product the identifier resolved to. Unset when error is set.

merged.title: merged
merged.description:
True when the identifier named a Product that was merged into another, and
 product is the surviving Product: the identifier you stored is stale, so
 store product.model_slug instead. This is the signal to rely on. Comparing
 product.model_slug with identifier is not, because a raw model number
 always differs from its slug. False when error is set.

error.title: error
error.description:
Why there is no product. Unset when product is set. Exactly one of product
 and error is present in every result.

drophawk.developer.v1.ProductResult.title: ProductResult
drophawk.developer.v1.ProductResult.description:
ProductResult is the answer for one requested identifier: the Product, or
 the reason there is none. Exactly one of product and error is set.

reason.title: reason
reason.description:
One of the reasons in the list on ProductService, the same ones the
 top-level ErrorInfo uses and that GET /v1/products/{model_slug} would have
 raised for this identifier: "PRODUCT_NOT_FOUND" (no Product is known by it,
 or it is no longer listed) or "INVALID_IDENTIFIER" (it cannot name any
 Product). More may be added within v1; treat an unrecognised reason as a
 failure to resolve this identifier.

drophawk.developer.v1.ProductResultError.title: ProductResultError
drophawk.developer.v1.ProductResultError.description: ProductResultError is why one identifier of a batch has no Product.

q.title: q
q.description:
The text to search for, such as "rtx 4090" or "asus tuf". Not blank, at
 most 256 bytes.

page_size.title: page_size
page_size.description:
The most Products to return. Defaults to 20 when 0 or omitted; a value over
 50 is treated as 50, and a negative value is an error.

page_token.title: page_token
page_token.description:
The next_page_token of the previous response, to get the page after it.
 Omit it for the first page.

client.title: client
client.description:
Which DropHawk surface is asking, so the buy_url it receives is attributed
 to that surface. "mcp" is honoured: the DropHawk MCP server sends it. Any
 other value, or none, means the API itself. The SDK sends nothing. It
 changes only buy_url, and nothing else about the response.

 Never rewrite a buy_url you were given: use it as is.

drophawk.developer.v1.SearchProductsRequ.title: SearchProductsRequest
drophawk.developer.v1.SearchProductsRequ.description: SearchProductsRequest is a text query and the page of its results to return.

products.title: products
products.description: The matching Products, best match first. Empty when nothing matches.

next_page_token.title: next_page_token
next_page_token.description:
Send this as page_token to get the next page. Empty when this is the last
 page.

drophawk.developer.v1.SearchProductsResp.title: SearchProductsResponse
drophawk.developer.v1.SearchProductsResp.description: SearchProductsResponse is one page of matching Products.

key.title: key
key.description:
The key of the Spec in Product.specs, for example "vram". Lowercase
 letters, digits and underscores.

label.title: label
label.description: A human-readable name for the Spec, for example "VRAM".

type.title: type
type.description:
The kind of value Product.specs holds under this key, which is the
 SpecValue field that carries it:

 - "string": text, in SpecValue.string_value.
 - "number": a number, in SpecValue.number_value.
 - "boolean": a yes/no value, in SpecValue.bool_value.

 More types may be added within v1, so the values listed in the schema are
 the known ones, not a closed set. A Product's specs never holds a value for
 a key whose type you do not recognise, so ignore such a Spec.

unit.title: unit
unit.description:
The unit the value is measured in, for example "GB" or "W", which a
 Product's SpecValue.unit repeats. Absent when the Spec has no unit.

drophawk.developer.v1.SpecField.title: SpecField
drophawk.developer.v1.SpecField.description: SpecField declares one Spec a ComponentType's Products can have.

unit.description: The unit the value is measured in, for example "GB" or "W". Absent when the attribute has no unit.

drophawk.developer.v1.SpecValue.title: SpecValue
drophawk.developer.v1.SpecValue.description:
SpecValue is one structured attribute of a Product. Exactly one of the value
 fields is set, matching the type the ComponentType declares for the key.

google.protobuf.Any.description:
One typed error detail: "@type" names its type, and the detail's own fields sit beside it.
The detail every HTTP/JSON error carries is google.rpc.ErrorInfo.

@type.description: The detail's type URL, for example "type.googleapis.com/google.rpc.ErrorInfo".

google.protobuf.Timestamp.description: A point in time in RFC 3339 format, with up to nanosecond precision. Output uses UTC (`Z`); input may use an offset from UTC.

google.rpc.ErrorInfo.description:
Why a request failed, as a machine-readable reason.
Every HTTP/JSON error carries one in its details; find it by its "@type".
The reasons are:

- PRODUCT_NOT_FOUND (404): no Product is known by the identifier, or it is no longer listed.
- INVALID_IDENTIFIER (400): the identifier cannot name any Product.
- INVALID_QUERY (400): the search query q is blank, over 256 bytes, or has control characters.
- INVALID_PAGE_TOKEN (400): the page_token is malformed, or was issued for a different q.
- INVALID_PAGE_SIZE (400): the page_size is negative.
- EMPTY_BATCH (400): a batch request names no identifiers.
- BATCH_TOO_LARGE (400): a batch request names more than 50 identifiers; metadata "max_identifiers" is the limit.
- INVALID_REQUEST (400): the request is malformed.
- NOT_FOUND (404): there is no such endpoint.
- METHOD_NOT_ALLOWED (405): the endpoint does not accept that HTTP method.
- REQUEST_TOO_LARGE (413): the request body is over 64 KiB. Retrying the same request cannot succeed; send less.
- RATE_LIMITED (429): too many requests; metadata "retry_after_seconds" repeats Retry-After.
- INTERNAL (500): DropHawk failed; retry later.
- UNAVAILABLE (503): DropHawk is briefly unable to serve; retry later.

More reasons may be added within v1. Treat an unrecognised reason by its HTTP status.

reason.description:
The reason, in UPPER_SNAKE_CASE.
The listed values are the known ones, not a closed set: more may be added within v1, so treat an unrecognised reason by its HTTP status.

metadata.description: Context for the reason, as string values.

code.description:
The google.rpc.Code of the error, for example 5 (NOT_FOUND) or 8 (RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED).
The HTTP status carries the same information.

message.description: The error code's name, such as "not_found", "resource_exhausted" or "internal". Not for display; branch on the ErrorInfo reason.

details.description:
Typed error details, each identified by its "@type".
An HTTP/JSON error always includes exactly one google.rpc.ErrorInfo naming why the request failed.
Other detail types may be added within v1; skip any whose "@type" you do not recognise.

get.description:
List every Brand that has at least one Product. A Brand with no Products is
 not listed.

200.description: Every Brand that has Products, ordered by name.

get.summary:
List every ComponentType: the classes of product DropHawk tracks, such as
 graphics cards or CPUs.
get.description:
Each entry carries the schema of the Specs its Products can have, which is
 the contract for the keys and value types of Product.specs: every key a
 Product returns in specs is declared in the spec_schema of its
 ComponentType, with a matching type. A ComponentType with no Products is
 still listed, with a product_count of 0.

get.summary: Get one Product by its model_slug.
get.description:
The identifier may also be the Product's raw model number as a store or the
 manufacturer writes it, for example "Deco X1500(1-pack)" (percent-encoded
 in the path). DropHawk maps it to a model_slug with its own rule, so do not
 assume which spellings it treats as the same: the response names the
 canonical model_slug, which is the value to store. A model number
 containing "/" cannot be sent this way, because a path segment cannot carry
 it even percent-encoded; send its model_slug instead.

 A Product that was found to duplicate another and merged into it answers
 301 Moved Permanently with a Location header naming the surviving Product's
 URL; follow it. A Product DropHawk does not know, or no longer lists,
 answers 404 with reason PRODUCT_NOT_FOUND.

parameters.name: model_slug
parameters.description: The Product's model_slug, or its raw model number. At most 256 bytes.

parameters.name: client
parameters.description:
Which DropHawk surface is asking, so the buy_url it receives is attributed
 to that surface. "mcp" is honoured: the DropHawk MCP server sends it. Any
 other value, or none, means the API itself. The SDK sends nothing. It
 changes only buy_url, and nothing else about the response.

 Never rewrite a buy_url you were given: use it as is.

get.summary: Get a Product's daily lows over the last 30 days.
get.description:
Each point is the lowest price DropHawk observed for the Product on one
 UTC calendar day, across all of its stores, whether or not a store had it
 in stock. It is not a history of best_price, which counts in-stock stores
 alone and is the price now: today's point can sit below today's
 best_price, and a day on which only an out-of-stock store was observed
 still has a point. A day on which no store was observed has no point, so
 the series can be sparse.

 The window is the current UTC day and the 29 before it. When the Product
 has an earlier point, the most recent one is also returned, marked
 is_carried_forward, so a Product last priced two months ago still has a
 price to chart. Draw it as the price in force at the window's start, and
 clip the line to the window.

 Prices in different currencies cannot be ranked against each other, so
 when the points in this series (the window and its carried-forward point)
 span more than one currency the series is withheld: points is empty and
 withheld_reason is "MIXED_CURRENCY". A Product with no history has an empty
 points list and withheld_reason "NO_DATA". These are the reasons of
 ProductPricing.all_time_low_withheld_reason, but judged on this series
 alone: an old price in another currency, outside the series, does not
 withhold it.

 The identifier is resolved exactly as for GET /v1/products/{model_slug},
 and so is a Product that was merged into another: 301 Moved Permanently
 with a Location header naming this endpoint for the surviving Product;
 follow it. A Product DropHawk does not know, or no longer lists, answers
 404 with reason PRODUCT_NOT_FOUND.

parameters.name: model_slug
parameters.description: The Product's model_slug, or its raw model number. At most 256 bytes.

200.description: The Product's daily lows, or why they are withheld.

post.summary: Get many Products in one call, such as the parts of a basket.
post.description:
Send up to 50 identifiers, each a model_slug or a raw model number exactly
 as GET /v1/products/{model_slug} accepts it. The response has one result
 per identifier you sent, in the order you sent them, so results[i] answers
 identifiers[i]. Duplicates are answered once each and are not an error.
 Every found Product is the same message GET /v1/products/{model_slug}
 returns, pricing included.

 An identifier that cannot be answered does not fail the call: its result
 carries no product and an error whose reason is PRODUCT_NOT_FOUND or
 INVALID_IDENTIFIER, the reasons the single GET would have raised. Branch on
 each result, not on the HTTP status, which is 200 whenever the request
 itself was acceptable.

 A Product that was merged into another resolves to the surviving Product
 here, with no redirect: its result has merged true and a product whose
 model_slug is the survivor's. Store that model_slug.

 A request with no identifiers answers 400 with reason EMPTY_BATCH, and one
 with more than 50 answers 400 with reason BATCH_TOO_LARGE; neither is
 partly served. The whole batch counts as one request against the rate limit,
 and, like every POST, its response is Cache-Control: no-store.

200.description: One result per requested identifier, in request order.

get.description:
q is matched against each Product's name, Brand name and model number,
 tolerating typos, case and punctuation, and results come best match first.
 Only listed Products are searched. A q with no matches is not an error: it
 returns an empty products list.

 Results are paginated. A response with more matches than page_size carries
 a next_page_token; send it back as page_token, with the same q, to get the
 following page. The last page has an empty next_page_token. Pages do not
 overlap and skip nothing while the catalog is unchanged; a Product added or
 removed between two requests can shift what a later page holds. A
 page_token is opaque, and only valid for the q it was issued for.

 Each Product is the same message GET /v1/products/{model_slug} returns,
 pricing included. A blank or malformed q answers 400 with reason
 INVALID_QUERY, a page_token that cannot be used answers 400 with reason
 INVALID_PAGE_TOKEN, and a negative page_size answers 400 with reason
 INVALID_PAGE_SIZE.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description:
The text to search for, such as "rtx 4090" or "asus tuf". Not blank, at
 most 256 bytes.

parameters.name: page_size
parameters.description:
The most Products to return. Defaults to 20 when 0 or omitted; a value over
 50 is treated as 50, and a negative value is an error.

parameters.name: page_token
parameters.description:
The next_page_token of the previous response, to get the page after it.
 Omit it for the first page.

parameters.name: client
parameters.description:
Which DropHawk surface is asking, so the buy_url it receives is attributed
 to that surface. "mcp" is honoured: the DropHawk MCP server sends it. Any
 other value, or none, means the API itself. The SDK sends nothing. It
 changes only buy_url, and nothing else about the response.

 Never rewrite a buy_url you were given: use it as is.

200.description: One page of matching Products, best match first.

tags.name: CatalogService
tags.description:
CatalogService lists the Brands and ComponentTypes that Products are
 organised by, and the Spec schema each ComponentType publishes.

 Both lists are small enough to return whole, so neither is paginated. It
 shares ProductService's host, rate limit, caching, cross-origin and error
 rules.

tags.name: ProductService
tags.description:
ProductService looks up Products and their prices.

 The API is served at https://api.drophawk.net. It needs no key: requests are
 anonymous, and an Authorization header is ignored.

 Each IP address may make 60 requests a minute on average, in bursts of up to
 30. RateLimit-Limit reports that burst (30), not the per-minute rate.
 RateLimit-Remaining and RateLimit-Reset report what is left of the burst and
 the seconds until it is full again; they are left off cacheable responses,
 because a cached response can be served to a different caller and costs
 nothing. A request over the limit gets 429 with Retry-After in seconds.

 One caching rule covers every protocol: a successful GET - an HTTP/JSON GET
 or HEAD, or a Connect GET - may be cached publicly for 5 minutes
 (Cache-Control: public, max-age=300). Every other response, any error and
 any POST included, is Cache-Control: no-store. Every response allows
 cross-origin requests from any web page (Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *).
 HEAD is answered like GET, without a body. Query parameters an endpoint does
 not define are ignored, so cache-busting and tracking parameters are
 harmless.

 One request field is meaningful beyond its endpoint's own: client. An agent
 tool that fronts this API (the DropHawk MCP server) sends client=mcp so the
 buy_url it is handed is attributed to that surface. Any other value, or none,
 is a direct API call. It is a query parameter or body field rather than a
 header, so it is part of the cache key.

 Every HTTP/JSON error is a google.rpc.Status whose details carry a
 google.rpc.ErrorInfo with domain "drophawk.net" and a reason. RPC callers
 (Connect, gRPC) get their protocol's own error model, carrying the same
 ErrorInfo whenever the API raised the error. Errors the RPC framework raises
 before the API sees the request carry none: a body that does not decode
 (invalid_argument, "invalid request body"), a request body over 64 KiB
 (resource_exhausted for an RPC caller, 413 REQUEST_TOO_LARGE over HTTP/JSON;
 never RATE_LIMITED, because retrying cannot help), or a method that does not
 exist. Branch on the reason, not on the message,
 which is the error code's name (for example "not_found" or "internal"). The
 reasons are:

 - "PRODUCT_NOT_FOUND" (404): no Product is known by the identifier, or it is
   no longer listed.
 - "INVALID_IDENTIFIER" (400): the identifier cannot name any Product.
 - "INVALID_QUERY" (400): the search query q is blank, over 256 bytes, or has
   control characters.
 - "INVALID_PAGE_TOKEN" (400): the page_token is malformed, or was issued for a
   different q.
 - "INVALID_PAGE_SIZE" (400): the page_size is negative.
 - "EMPTY_BATCH" (400): a batch request names no identifiers.
 - "BATCH_TOO_LARGE" (400): a batch request names more than 50 identifiers;
   metadata "max_identifiers" is the limit.
 - "INVALID_REQUEST" (400): the request is malformed.
 - "NOT_FOUND" (404): there is no such endpoint.
 - "METHOD_NOT_ALLOWED" (405): the endpoint does not accept that HTTP method.
 - "REQUEST_TOO_LARGE" (413): the request body is over 64 KiB. Retrying the same
   request cannot succeed; send less.
 - "RATE_LIMITED" (429): too many requests; metadata "retry_after_seconds"
   repeats Retry-After.
 - "INTERNAL" (500): DropHawk failed; retry later.
 - "UNAVAILABLE" (503): DropHawk is briefly unable to serve; retry later.

 More reasons may be added within v1. Treat an unrecognised reason by its HTTP
 status.
